sample_unit: structured yes/no questions (600 responses per model over three weekly sessions)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated weekly sessions (Fleiss' and Cohen's kappa)
links.effect: ChatGPT showed near-perfect reproducibility (kappa = 0.95); Gemini showed only fair agreement (kappa = 0.38). Accuracy was 92.8% vs. 84.8%.
links.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated significantly higher overall accuracy than Gemini (92.8% vs. 84.8%; OR = 2.37; p = 0.004) and near-perfect reproducibility (κ = 0.95), whereas Gemini showed fair agreement (κ = 0.38).

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on guideline-derived endodontic yes/no items, by clinical domain
links.effect: Overall accuracy was 92.8% (ChatGPT) and 84.8% (Gemini). Both models performed well in structured domains but had reduced accuracy in restoration and pulpal disease management.
links.quote: Both models performed well in structured clinical domains but showed reduced accuracy in areas related to restoration and pulpal disease management.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy, consistency, and temporal stability of LLMs on endodontic questions derived from guidelines, but does not test any deployment practices or organizational safeguards.
